Common adverse effects of valganciclovir include abdominal pain (15%), anemia (8–26%), diarrhea (16–41%), fever (31%), granulocytopenia (11–27%), headache (9–22%), insomnia (16%), nausea (8–30%), retinal detachment (15%), vomiting (21%), peripheral neuropathy (9%), paresthesia (8%), and thrombocytopenia (8%). Other reported effects include pyrexia, fatigue, tremor, neutropenia, leukopenia, urinary tract infections, anaphylactic reactions, agranulocytosis, and pancytopenia. 78. Hematologic toxicity associated with valganciclovir includes severe leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopenia, and bone marrow failure, including aplastic anemia. 79. Valganciclovir may impair fertility based on animal and limited human data. It may cause temporary or permanent inhibition of spermatogenesis in males and suppression of fertility in females. 80. Fetal toxicity is a concern with valganciclovir, as animal data suggest it may cause birth defects in humans. 81. Valganciclovir has mutagenic and carcinogenic potential based on animal studies, indicating a risk of cancer development in humans. 82. Patients with a history of hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis) to valganciclovir, ganciclovir, or excipients should avoid this medication. 83. Valganciclovir may be teratogenic or embryotoxic. Female patients of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 30 days afterward. Male patients should use barrier methods during treatment and for at least 90 days afterward to minimize fetal risk. 84. Acute renal failure may occur in elderly patients, even in the absence of pre-existing renal dysfunction. Caution is advised when administering valganciclovir to this population.
